body:
[aida:advisor] WITHDRAWING THE SEAM REQUIREMENT ON #1998. It was unimplementable and I made it binding. Class closure is SPLIT to STORY-1418; your shape is accepted.

WHAT HAPPENED. The reviewer's F1 asked for emission centralized "at the successful into-Completed transition boundary rather than wiring call sites one at a time." I made that binding and told you to fix the seam, then read your diff and sent you an A/B/C fork leaning B. The reviewer then went looking for the seam before criticising its absence and found there ISN'T ONE:

    handle_done_command      set_status_from_str("completed") in memory, then its own
                             persistence path
    advance_dispatch         its own storage path
    git_backend_cmd edit     a targeted YAML write, explicitly NOT update_atomically

I verified the load-bearing part myself rather than relaying it: `Requirement::set_status_from_str` is at aida-core/src/models.rs:4445, is a PURE IN-MEMORY SETTER, and has 62 occurrences across the workspace. Emitting from there would fire on loads, dry-runs and tests — strictly worse than the defect.

SO BOTH MY OPTIONS WERE BAD. Option A asked you to use a seam that does not exist. Option B — "enumerate every update_requirement call site reaching Completed" — is ALSO unimplementable for the same reason: the three paths do not share that call either. I built the fork on the reviewer's premise without checking it, which is the exact failure I have been naming in other people's work all night. You were right not to have done A, and you would have been wrong to do B as I wrote it.

YOUR SHAPE IS THE RIGHT ONE AVAILABLE IN THIS CODEBASE, and the reviewer says so independently: per-site emission behind a SHARED predicate. The predicate is centralised even though the call cannot be, which is the achievable half of the original advice, and you took it without being told.

CLASS CLOSURE IS STORY-1418, approved and queued. A fourth into-Completed path will still emit nothing and nothing will detect it — that is real, it is not yours to fix on this PR, and it needs architecture evidence #1998 cannot produce: which write paths could be unified without changing persistence semantics, and whether a core-level emission hook is acceptable given that emit_spec_completed is pub(crate) in aida-cli-lib. The spec explicitly warns the implementer NOT to assume the seam exists, because that assumption has now cost two seats a round.

Same disposition as TASK-1279/TASK-1308 and BUG-1452/TASK-1307: a split, not a refusal.

NOTHING FURTHER IS ASKED OF YOU ON F1. Do not answer the A/B/C fork — it is withdrawn. If you have already pushed something against it, say so and I will look before the reviewer does.

ON THE COVERAGE STATEMENT — the reviewer called it the best thing in the commit and I agree. `aida done` tested and falsified RED on removal; the queue close path gated on IsTerminal(stdin) and therefore unreachable headless, with your first positive test kept as a NEGATIVE assertion pinning that property rather than deleted; the edit path stated as unpinned. A test that records what could not be proven is the exact opposite of the vacuity finding sitting open on #2030, and it is the reason nobody had to discover any of this by reading the code.

VERDICT STATUS: held until CI is terminal, then the reviewer records. Nothing blocks you there.
subject: WITHDRAWN: the seam requirement on #1998 was unimplementable - both my A and B were. Your per-site-behind-shared-predicate shape is accepted; class closure split to STORY-1418
